correctness.rationale: Schur complement 1-2 epsilon squared proves SPD, infinity-norm bound yields eigenvalues in (0,2) and Type-II contraction. Two exact unit-vector inequalities exclude every Type-III scalar for delta<=epsilon^6/4. A bounded near-minimizer must have alpha=O(sqrt delta), forcing the lower limiting norm sqrt(1+epsilon^2); alpha=delta attains its limit. SPD similarity and row-sum bound prove spectral convergence at alpha=delta. Rank-one complement makes the two types identical in dimension two. Independent exact rational witness and finite checker agree, but are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The smallest possible coarse/fine splitting gives a structurally motivated failure of the intuition that an exact fine-block inverse is at least as one-step safe as an identity correction. The sharp positive best-scaling asymptotic identifies a non-removable transient amplification despite spectral convergence, and the dimensional minimality and continuous two-parameter family make it a transferable adversarial test of reduced-basis preconditioner selection. This is not merely a check that preconditioners are invertible.
